short: The son of James II who spent his life in exile attempting to reclaim the British throne.
full:
Born in 1688, James Francis Edward Stuart was the son of the Catholic King James II. His birth precipitated the Glorious Revolution, which saw his father deposed and replaced by William III and Mary II. Raised in exile in France and Italy, James became the "Old Pretender", recognized by Jacobites and several Catholic powers as the rightful King James III of England and VIII of Scotland.

He orchestrated several attempts to regain the thrones, most notably the Jacobite rising of 1715, but lacked the necessary domestic support and military fortune. After the failure of the '15, he settled in Rome under papal protection, where he maintained a shadow court until his death in 1766, having passed his political ambitions to his son, Charles Edward Stuart.
